(7) Body dimensions as to length and height of front-loading containers can vary with the size of container; however, all container widths will be 70 inches. Minimum gauges of steel shall be as follows:
Walls | 12 gauge
Ends | 12 gauge
Bottoms | 12 gauge for 4 cu. yd. and below
| 10 gauge for all over 4 cu. yd.
Lids | 16 gauge or equivalent strength plastic
Doors | 14 gauge
Commercial establishment means any hotel, motel, trailer/mobile home parks, apartment house, rooming house, rental property of two or more multiple-dwelling units, business, retail stores, industrial, public or semipublic establishment of any nature or kind whatsoever other than a single dwelling unit/residential unit and condominiums.
Commercial/industrial refuse means waste material from industrial processes, manufacturing, canneries, slaughterhouses, packing plants, poultry processing or similar industries, and large quantities of condemned foods. The term "commercial refuse" also includes waste material from the construction, remodeling and repair operations on houses, commercial buildings, multiple-dwellings and other structures and includes such materials as concrete, bricks, plaster, stone, earth, lumber, roofing materials, gutters, shavings and sawdust.
Compactor container means a manufactured commercial container of a specified size with a self-contained compacting mechanism or an external compactor which is designed to be used in conjunction with the disposal/collection system.
Composting means the controlled biological decomposition of organic waste.
Condominium means individual ownership units in a multifamily structure with a front and back entrance to each unit on the ground level.
Construction/demolition waste means the waste building materials and rubble resulting from construction, remodeling, repair, and demolition operations associated with such things as pavements, houses, commercial buildings and other structures. Such wastes include, but are not limited to wood, bricks, metal, concrete, wallboard, paper or cardboard.
Convenience center means a county disposal site where county residents deposit refuse by type (i.e., household, yard, white goods and furniture, and recyclables) for collection and disposal/processing by the county sanitation department.
Department means the county sanitation department.
Disposal facility means any facility or location where any treatment, utilization, processing or disposition of solid waste occurs as licensed/permitted by the state through the department of natural resources.
Disposal operation means the performance of solid waste disposal, which includes administration, personnel, land, equipment, design, and other elements necessary or used in the work of solid waste disposal.
Disposal site means the location where the final disposition of solid waste occurs.
Division means the environmental protection division of the Georgia Department of Natural Resources.
Garbage means food waste, including waste accumulations of animal or vegetable matter used or intended for use as food or that attends the preparation, use, cooking, dealing in or storing of meat, fish, fowl, fruit or vegetables.
Hazardous waste means any solid waste which has been defined as a hazardous waste in regulations promulgated by the board of natural resources for the state.
Incineration means a controlled process by which solid, liquid and gaseous combustible wastes are burned and changed into gases and a residue produced which is relatively free of combustible materials.
Incinerator means all devices intended or used for the reduction or destruction of solid, liquid or gaseous waste by burning.
Industrial waste means solid waste generated by manufacturing or industrial processes that is not a hazardous waste as defined herein.
Inert waste landfill means a disposal site accepting only wastes that will not or are not likely to cause production of leachate of environmental concern. Such wastes are limited to dirt and dirt-like products, concrete, rock, bricks, yard trimmings, stumps, limbs, and leaves. This definition excludes industrial and demolition waste.
Infectious waste means all biomedical waste as defined in Solid Waste Management Rules of the State of Georgia.
Leachate means a liquid that has passed through or emerged from solid waste and contains soluble, suspended, or miscible materials removed from such wastes.
Liquid waste means any waste material that is determined to contain "free liquids" as defined by Method 9095 (Paints Filter Liquids Test), as described in "Test Methods of Evaluation of Solid Wastes, Physical/Chemical Methods" (EPA Pub. No. SW-846).
Litter means all garbage, refuse, waste materials, sand, gravel, slag, brickbats, rubbish, tin cans, trash, debris, dead animals, or any other discarded substance which is not handled in accordance with the provisions of this chapter.
Medical waste means all biomedical waste as defined in this section.
Mulch means shredded material, such as pine needles, tree branches and leaves, wood products which have not been painted, treated, or contaminated by any substance in any form or fashion, which is used to prevent erosion of soils and/or the evaporation of ground moisture from plant beds. Mulch differs from compost in that it has not been subjected to decomposition processes as herein defined and is not composed of materials classified as putrescible wastes.
Multiple-dwelling means a building designed for and containing two or more dwelling units.
Noncombustible trash means materials which are unburnable in an incinerator or at incinerator temperatures of 800 to 1,800 degrees Fahrenheit (i.e., mineral matter, metal furniture, large metal scraps and wire).
Nuisance means anything which meets the definition of the term as defined by O.C.G.A. § 41-1-1 and which occurs during or as a result of the handling or disposing of solid waste.
Open dump means an unpermitted disposal site at which solid waste from one or more sources is consolidated and left to decompose, burn or to otherwise create a threat to human health or the environment.
Operator means the person having direct supervision of daily field operation of a disposal site to ensure that the site operates in compliance with the permit.
Owner means any person owning, leasing, renting, occupying or managing any premises in the jurisdiction of the board of county commissioners.
Person means the State of Georgia or any other state or any agency or institution thereof, and any municipality, political subdivision, public or private corporation, special district empowered to engage in solid waste management activities, individual, partnership, association or other entity in Georgia or any other state. The term "person" also includes any officer or governing or managing body of any municipality, political subdivision, special district empowered in solid waste activities, or public or private corporation in Georgia or any other state. The term "person" also includes employees, departments, and agencies of the federal government.
Plastic bag means a polyethylene or other heavy-duty plastic bag meeting the National Sanitation Foundation standard of at least 1.5 mils and not exceeding a 30-gallon capacity, with securing twist or pull ties. An untied bag shall not be an approved container.
Putrescible wastes means wastes that are capable of being quickly decomposed by microorganisms. Examples of putrescible wastes include but are not necessarily limited to kitchen wastes, animal manure, offal, hatchery and poultry processing plant wastes, and garbage.
Recyclable means any waste stream product which can be reclaimed and reprocessed by others into its original or modified form for reuse.
Recycling means any process by which reclaimed materials or other materials which would otherwise become solid waste are collected, separated, or processed and reused or returned to use in the form of raw materials or products.
Recycling center means the county facility where recyclables are collected from various areas of the county, segregated by type, and processed for market distribution.
Recycling container means a specifically designated container, normally identified with the recycling logo into which recyclable products are placed as specifically designated on the container.
Refuse means garbage, rubbish or commercial refuse.
Residential unit means any freestanding structure or shelter or any part thereof used or constructed for use as a residence for one family.
Rubbish means wastepaper, cartons, boxes, wood, tree branches, yard trimmings, furniture, appliances, metals, cans, glass, crockery, dunnage, and/or similar materials.
Sanitary landfill means a disposal site where putrescible solid wastes are disposed of by means of placing an earth cover thereon, as permitted by the state through the environmental protection division.
Sanitary landfilling means an engineered method of disposing of putrescible solid wastes on land by spreading the waste in thin layers, compacting the waste to the smallest practical volume, placing an earth cover thereon and such other measures as are necessary to protect human health and the environment.
Scavenge means the uncontrolled picking from discarded solid waste materials.
Scavenger, private contractor, or commercial sanitation firm means any person other than a municipality, who is licensed by the county to collect, remove, salvage or dispose of refuse from one or more public or private premises, other than the person's own, whether or not under written contract, and whether or not for compensation.
Solid waste means putrescible and nonputrescible wastes, except water-carried body waste and materials destined for recycling, and shall include garbage, rubbish (paper, cartons, boxes, wood, tree branches, yard trimmings, furniture, and appliances, metal, tin cans, glass, crockery, or dunnage), ashes, street refuse, dead animals, sewage sludges, animal manures, industrial wastes (waste materials generated from industrial operations) residue from incineration, food processing wastes, demolition wastes, and other waste material in solid or semi-solid state not otherwise defined in this chapter or by the state.
Solid waste enterprise fund means a self-sufficient, revenue-producing fund and full cost accounting system which encompasses the total cost of solid waste disposal operations of the county as managed by the board of commissioners, thereby preventing subsidizing the cost of solid waste disposal operations from the county's general fund.
Solid waste handling means the storage, collection, transportation, treatment, utilization, processing, or disposal of solid waste, or any combination thereof.
Solid waste handling facility means any location where any storage, collection, transportation, treatment, utilization, processing or disposal of solid waste or any combination thereof occurs.
Solid waste handling permit means written authorization granted to a person by the director, EPD, DNR, of the State of Georgia to engage in solid waste handling.
Solid Waste Management Act or the Act refers to O.C.G.A. § 12-8-20.
Solid waste task force means a board of persons appointed by the board of commissioners to oversee the solid waste management operations of the county. Board membership is composed of one member from each incorporated municipality within the county, two county commissioners, the county administrator, the clean community coordinator, local business leaders, the industrial authority, school board representatives, and the sanitation department supervisor. The task force reviews solid waste policies within the county and makes recommendations for policy changes to the board of county commissioners.
Special solid waste means any solid waste not otherwise regulated under the Georgia Hazardous Waste Management Act, O.C.G.A. § 12-8-60 et seq., and regulations promulgated thereunder or originating or produced from or by a source or generator not subject to regulation under O.C.G.A. § 12-8-27(g).
Trailer/mobile home park means a parcel of land owned by an individual, partnership, or corporation used or set apart for the purpose of supplying parking space for two or more mobile homes and which includes buildings, structures, vehicles, or enclosures used or intended for use as a part of such a park.
Transfer station means a facility used to transfer solid waste from one transportation vehicle to another for transportation to a disposal site or processing operation.

(a) It shall be unlawful for any person, including county refuse collectors and sanitary contractors, to haul, convey or cause to be conveyed any refuse, including discarded building materials or discarded furniture, upon or along the public streets and roadways except when the material transported is adequately secured in such a manner as to prevent its falling, leaking, or being blown from the transporting vehicle. 791:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person to dump or cause to be dumped any garbage, refuse, litter, junk, appliances, equipment, cans, bottles, paper, lumber, trees, tree limbs, brush or parts thereof anywhere in the jurisdictional area of the county except at the sanitary landfill, dry trash landfill or transfer station operated by the county or as may be permitted elsewhere in these regulations without the expressed approval by action of the board of commissioners under such terms and conditions as may be invoked from time to time by the board.
(b) The provisions of subsection (a) of this section do not apply to the dumping on private property of sand, dirt, broken concrete, blocks, bricks, broken pavement sections, or other suitable material for use as fill to raise the elevation of the land, provided the owner possesses a state-approved permit to operate an inert landfill; and providing the owner has given permission, and provided it is not maintained in an unsightly condition and provided the owner of the property on which such material is dumped agrees to level such dumped material with appropriate equipment and assess the cost thereof against the real property on which such material is dumped. This section is not to be construed as authority to fill or modify wetlands which is governed by the corps of engineers.
(c) If any of the matter or material dumped in violation of the provisions of subsection (a) of this section can be identified as having last belonged to, been in the possession of, sent to or received by, or to have been the property of any person prior to its being dumped as prohibited herein, this identification shall be presumed to be prima facie evidence that the owner dumped or caused to be dumped such matter and material in violation of this chapter.
(d) For information leading to the arrest and conviction of any person violating the provisions of this chapter or the provisions of any state law prohibiting the dumping of garbage, refuse, or litter on any public or private property within the county, the board may, in its discretion, pay a reward in the amount established by action of the board of commissioners, a copy of which is on file in the office of the county administrator, to the person furnishing such information leading to such arrest and conviction and such monies as may be a necessary cost of the operation and administration of the county government.
(e) All compactors containing combustible materials emptied at a county disposal facility will pay the price per ton established in section 34-45. These fees may be changed from time to time by resolution of the governing authority of the county.

(g) No person shall place any refuse, trash, refuse receptacle or container on, over, or near any storm drain or drainage, ditches, or so close thereto as to cause such material to interfere in any way with such drainage.

Failure of the owner or occupant to remove and correct any such accumulation of refuse after appropriate notice from the county shall raise the presumption that such person intended to violate the article.
(i) It shall be unlawful for any person to place or leave outside any building or dwelling except as specified in this subsection any dilapidated furniture, appliance, machinery, equipment, building material, junked motor vehicle, or other items which is either in a partially rusted, wrecked, junked, dismantled, or inoperative condition, and which is not completely enclosed within a building or dwelling. Any such item or items which remain on the property of the occupant for a period of 30 days after notice of violation of this section, shall be presumed to be abandoned and subject to being removed from the property by the county without further notice. The county may charge the owner or occupant a fee for the cost of removing said item or items. This section shall not apply to licensed junk dealers or currently licensed establishments engaged in the repair, rebuilding, reconditioning or salvaging of equipment or furniture.
(j) It shall be unlawful for any person to leave outside any building in a place accessible to children any appliance, refrigerator, or other container which has an airtight snap lock or similar device without first removing therefrom the lock or door. This section shall not apply to any appliances, refrigerators or container which has been placed on or adjacent to the rear of the building and which has been crated, strapped or locked so that it will be impossible for a child to obtain access to any compartment thereof.
(k) No person other than the owner thereof or an agent or employee of the county/municipality shall disturb or interfere with any container used for the purpose of storing refuse pending the collection, or remove any contents therefrom or remove such container from its location.

801:
(a) County convenience centers. The county shall divide the unincorporated areas of the county into pickup routes and convenience center locations. The routes and convenience center locations shall be plainly outlined on a map of the county and numbered alpha-numerically. The county shall prepare a list of the names of all streets, roads, alleys, drives, highways, and other public thoroughfares which form each route; shall keep the map and list for public inspection; and shall furnish a copy of the map showing any particular route and convenience center along with a list of names of the public thoroughfares therein to any person who requests them upon the payment of the actual cost for the reproduction of the map and list by either a county or commercial facility, whichever is available.

802:
The county will operate appropriate convenience centers approved by the board of commissioners. Normally, a convenience center will provide bulk collection containers for household solid waste (putrescible); recyclables; yard waste on a specified scheduled basis; and large household items such as furniture and appliances on a specified scheduled basis. Each convenience center will have posted the hours of operation. It shall be the duty of the occupant or owner of any private residential unit to properly maintain all refuse pending disposal at one of the county-operated convenience centers or to transport such refuse to the county-operated sanitary landfill, dry trash landfill, transfer station or other private disposal facility as herein defined.
(1) All residential garbage shall be free of liquid and placed in watertight paper or plastic bags and the tops secured and placed in appropriate waste containers at designated county convenience centers.
(2) All county residents governed by these regulations will be encouraged, through educational programs and community pride, to participate in the county recycling program. Each resident is encouraged to separate recyclables from residential waste prior to disposal and to voluntarily deposit recyclables at the nearest convenience center.
(3) Other household refuse, less recyclables, will be containerized where practical and disposed of at one of the county convenience centers based upon the posted hours. Such refuse will not be disposed of at any convenience center unless the designated type of refuse container is available at the center. Refuse improperly deposited will be classified as litter and handled as regulated herein.
(4) Household yard wastes will be accepted at convenience centers; however, such waste shall not exceed four feet in length nor be any larger than four inches in diameter. Such yard waste shall fit into the available container. Yard waste improperly deposited at any county facility shall be treated as litter and handled as regulated herein.
(5) Each owner shall prevent the continued, excessive and unsightly accumulation of refuse upon the property such person occupies or the public thoroughfares adjoining the property.
(6) It shall be unlawful to place or cause to be placed in any refuse collection container any lead acid or mercury battery, engine or hydraulic oils, explosive material, flammable liquid, inflatable rubber tires of any size, liquid in excess of one U.S. gallon, or dangerous or corrosive material of any kind. (Disposal of such materials shall be coordinated with the clean community coordinator.)
(7) Inoperative, privately used, worn-out household appliances (refrigerators, stoves, washing machines, dryers, freezers, air conditioners, furniture) will be collected at convenience centers on specified dates.
(8) Household waste (yard, appliances, construction debris) generated by a private single residence may be delivered directly to the county-operated sanitary landfill or the transfer station at no charge to the resident.
(9) Commercial or construction waste generated from the conduct of business or commercial enterprise carried on from or at private residential units will not be disposed of at county convenience centers. Such waste shall be disposed of as commercial or construction waste as regulated elsewhere in this chapter.
(Code 1987, § 15-28; Ord. of 11-3-1992)
803:
(a) All commercial establishments, condominiums, and townhouses within the county shall be required to provide for commercial collection/disposal of all solid waste, except for recyclables, when no recycling container is provided at such locations. It shall be unlawful for commercially generated waste to be disposed of at any county-operated convenience center.

(2) Furniture.
(3) Tires.

(6) Bed springs.
(7) Rock, dirt, concrete blocks, etc.

(j) All loading and unloading areas shall be provided with refuse receptacles for loose debris, paper, packaging materials and other trash. The owner or occupant of the commercial establishment or multidwelling unit shall place a sufficient number of containers in said area to maintain a clean, neat, and sanitary condition at all times.
(k) All parking lots and establishments with parking lots shall provide refuse receptacles within the parking area. Such receptacles shall be weighed or attached to the ground as necessary to prevent spillage. It shall be the responsibility of the owner or his agent to collect the refuse and trash deposited in such containers and store this material in a location until collected by the county. The sanitation department supervisor shall have the authority to determine the number and types of receptacles necessary to provide property containerization.
(l) It shall be the obligation of all persons using the parking areas to place any trash or litter in receptacles or containers, and it shall be unlawful for any person to dump, scatter or throw on any parking lot, any refuse, garbage or trash of any kind.
(m) All construction and demolition contractors shall provide on-site refuse receptacles, bulk containers or detachable containers for the collection of loose debris, paper, building material waste, scrap building materials, and other trash produced by those working at the construction/demolition site. All such sites shall be kept in a litter-free condition. The number and size of the containers will be determined by the volume of refuse generated and the size of the site. Dirt, mud, construction materials, or other debris upon any public or private property belonging to a person other than the owner of the construction site shall be removed by the contractor upon completion of the construction.
(Code 1987, § 15-29; Ord. of 11-3-1992)
804:
(a) Refuse may be collected for disposal by the county by municipalities, or by persons or commercial sanitation firms licensed by the state and either the county or municipality for which the service is contracted.
(b) The county and its licensed scavengers will collect refuse under the following conditions:
(1) Convenience centers for residential (noncommercial) county residents.
a. Refuse will be collected from county-operated convenience centers at least weekly. Collection frequency will be determined by the volume or refuse disposed of at each center.
b. Recycling containers will be spotted at each convenience center on a scheduled weekly basis. These containers will accept recyclables such as glass, plastic, and aluminum.
c. A newspaper recycling container will be available at each center on a continuous basis.
d. Containers for yard waste and white goods, furniture, and large bulky items of residential use will be spotted at each convenience center on a scheduled weekly basis.
e. Dead animals, regardless of size, will not be collected at convenience centers. Dead animals (household pets) will be disposed of at the animal shelter. Large dead animals shall be disposed of by burial on the individual's property to whom the animal belongs. The county has no responsibility to supply service for the removal and disposal of large dead animals.
f. The county shall not be responsible for the collection or hauling of discarded building materials, dirt, rock, discarded furniture, or appliances from private property, nor shall it be responsible for collecting or hauling trees, bushes, other vegetation or debris generated from commercial or residential occupant tree trimming, landscaping, or construction activities.
(2) Commercial and multiple-dwelling units.
a. Refuse will be collected as often as seven times per week. Frequency of pickup will be determined by the county sanitation department supervisor and the local health department based on generation volumes, available container capacity, container type, and type of refuse.
b. Commercial establishments choosing to recycle specific items will containerize the recyclables as specified in the recycling agreement. Recyclables will be collected at least weekly.
(Code 1987, § 15-30; Ord. of 11-3-1992)
805:
The board of commissioners recommends monthly billings of all accounts.
(Code 1987, § 15-31; Ord. of 11-3-1992)
806:
(a) The solid waste management fees will be charged based on the service provided and shall be in amounts as established by the board of commissioners from time to time.
(b) Municipalities that provide collection services will be charged on a per-ton basis for the amount of waste disposed. The total fee for municipalities providing collection will be per-ton and in an amount as established by the board of commissioners from time to time.
(c) The unincorporated areas of the county and municipalities that do not provide collection will be charged based on a per capita basis for collection and disposal instead of tipping fees. This includes municipalities that provide collection but also have county-maintained dumpsters within their city limits which are used for residential customers. This fee is based on per capita which is a pro-rata share of the fees and will be in an amount as established by the board of commissioners from time to time.
(d) Contractors who deliver waste to the county landfill or transfer station will be charged the same as municipalities providing collection.
(e) Charges for disposal of yard waste will be on a per-ton basis. The fees for disposal of yard waste shall be in an amount as established by the board of commissioners from time to time.
(f) Charges for disposal of building construction material will be on a per-ton basis. The fees for disposal of building construction material shall be in amounts as established by the board of commissioners from time to time.
(g) Charges for disposal of white goods will be on a per-ton basis. The fees for disposal of white goods shall be in amounts as established by the board of commissioners from time to time.
(Code 1987, § 15-32; Ord. of 11-3-1992)
809:
(a) The full costs of providing all or a portion of the residential solid waste services in the county shall be recovered from the citizens thereof, who benefit from the availability of county provided services, in the form of a solid waste assessment and/or a solid waste tipping fee. The solid waste cost components include collection of residential putrescible and bulk waste, disposal of residential putrescible and bulk waste, transfer station operations, debt service, recycling, landfill closure and post closure maintenance, litter control, polycart service where provided, and the "Keep Liberty Beautiful" program.
(b) The revenue derived from the solid waste assessment shall be set to cover the costs of solid waste services provided to the respective tax districts of the county.
(c) The solid waste tipping fees shall be set to cover the full costs of the county waste disposal.
(d) The amount to be charged as the solid waste assessment and the solid waste tipping fees shall be established and adjusted as necessary by the county board of commissioners, and shall appear in the official minutes of the board meeting at which the charges are adopted by resolution. At that time, they shall constitute a fee schedule and become attached to this article.
(Code 1987, § 15-101; Ord. No. 2004-002, 12-7-2004; Ord. No. 2006-002, 2-1-2006; Ord. No. 2007-004, 12-4-2007)
810:
There shall be a solid waste assessment imposed on all privately owned, single-family residential properties and camper lots located in the county to recover the costs associated with solid waste services provided by the county solid waste. There are eight tax districts in the county: Seven corresponding to the seven municipalities of the county and one for the unincorporated area of the county. The solid waste assessment will vary by tax district, based on the level of solid waste services offered by the specific governing body of the tax district and the county board of commissioners. The solid waste assessment will be collected as part of the annual county tax billing process in the same manner as prescribed for collection of said tax bill.
(Code 1987, § 15-102; Ord. No. 2004-002, 12-7-2004; Ord. No. 2006-002, 2-1-2006; Ord. No. 2014-003, 3-4-2014; Ord. No. 2019-003, 7-18-2019)
811:
(a) The solid waste assessment will be collected as follows: Individual, single-family, and private residential units in the county will be billed under the following tax districts at the rates as cited in section 34-71:
Unincorporated Liberty County | Tax District 1
Hinesville | Tax District 2
Allenhurst | Tax District 3
Flemington | Tax District 4
Gumbranch | Tax District 5
Midway | Tax District 6
Riceboro | Tax District 7
Walthourville | Tax District 8
(b) Individual single-family, private residential properties will be billed as part of their annual property tax bill for the annual solid waste assessment. The annual solid waste assessment is not a tax, it is an assessment. As such the assessment is not based upon the taxable value of the residence but is an annual fee imposed equally on each specified property within the specific tax district.
(c) The solid waste assessment for camper lots will be billed annually based on occupancy of the lot as of January of the calendar year for which the solid waste assessment covers, regardless of tax district.
(1) The county tax commissioner will include the solid waste assessment with the property tax bill of all private, residential properties located in each county tax district. The tax commissioner will maintain a solid waste assessment billing register. Sixty days after the due date for the solid waste assessment, the tax commissioner will send a delinquency notice to each residential property owner who has not paid their correct solid waste billing. This notice will advise payment is due within 30 days or the delinquent account will be sent to the magistrate court for collection. Upon expiration of the 30-day delinquency notice time period, the tax commissioner will transmit a copy of the delinquent solid waste assessment billing register to the county board of commissioners for collection effort.
(2) Upon receipt of the delinquent solid waste assessment billing register, the board of commissioners will prepare all necessary documentation for processing collection through the magistrate's court for collection of the delinquent solid waste assessment fees.
(3) Delinquent solid waste assessment fees, as recorded on the delinquent register shall be deemed past due and delinquent, and will be charged a late fee equal to one percent, compounded monthly.
(Code 1987, § 15-103; Ord. No. 2004-002, 12-7-2004; Ord. No. 2006-002, 2-1-2006; Ord. No. 2007-004, 12-4-2007; Ord. No. 2014-003, 3-4-2014)
812:
Private, single-family residential property owners who have contracted with a licensed (EPD permitted) contractor for polycart service of household garbage may, upon proof of annual contract with the service provider, request reduction of their solid waste assessment by the household waste component cost of the solid waste assessment. If such private service has been for less than the billing year, the solid waste assessment will be reduced proportionately.
(Code 1987, § 15-104; Ord. No. 2004-002, 12-7-2004)
813:
(a) Units to be billed. Annually, the county board of commissioners, through the office of the county tax assessor, will determine the number of private residential units, by tax district, to be billed for the residential solid waste assessment.
(b) Exclusions.
(1) Commercial dwelling properties. Specifically excluded from this residential solid waste assessment are rental properties such as apartments, townhouses and mobile home or trailer parks. These residential properties are considered commercial enterprises and must provide full solid waste services for the individual residents of these complexes as detailed elsewhere in these ordinances. Residents of these rental properties are prohibited for using rural residential waste disposal facilities or commercial/business waste disposal containers provided by businesses other than containers provided by the owner of the rental property specified in this section. Fines for violation of this provision of the ordinance are detailed in section 34-70.
(2) Low income senior citizens. Senior citizens classified on the county tax assessor's tax base as S-4, tax exempt, who earn $25,000.00 or less per annum, who are the sole source of income for the specific residential property, and who submit verifiable supporting documentation to the tax assessor's office by March 1 each calendar year, will be exempt from payment of the solid waste assessment for the next solid waste billing cycle.
(Code 1987, § 15-105; Ord. No. 2004-002, 12-7-2004; Ord. No. 2007-004, 12-4-2007)
814:
(a) There shall be a solid waste tipping fee imposed to recover the costs of siting, engineering, construction, operation, landfill closure and post-closure maintenance and monitoring, haul and disposal of the waste stream, and operation of the county solid waste transfer station. This solid waste tipping fee will be imposed on all public sector, private sector and commercial customers using the county transfer station (disposal facility).
(b) The solid waste tipping fee imposed upon all users of the county transfer station (disposal facility) shall be in accord with the fee as cited in section 34-71.
(c) The solid waste tipping fee as cited in section 34-71 for municipalities is established as Level 1, Level 2, and Level 3. These fee levels are based on the respective community's past commitment to the county solid waste. The following details the tipping fee charges for respective county municipalities:
(1) Level 1: Hinesville, Flemington and Walthourville.
(2) Level 2: Allenhurst, Gumbranch and Riceboro.
(3) Level 3: Midway.
(d) The exact transactional dollar amount of each solid waste tipping fee billing shall be determined at the solid waste transfer station through a measurement system using either weight, volume, or count, depending upon the type of solid waste being delivered to the facility, in accord with the solid waste tipping fees as cited in section 34-71.
(e) Payment of the transacted solid waste tipping fee will be cash, check or charge for prearranged customer accounts.
(f) Invoices shall be sent monthly by the county solid waste department to all solid waste tipping fee account holders, and shall be deemed past due and delinquent 30 days after receipt of said invoices. A late charge of 1.5 percent, compounded monthly, will be assessed against all delinquent amounts.
(Code 1987, § 15-106; Ord. No. 2004-002, 12-7-2004; Ord. No. 2006-002, 2-1-2006; Ord. No. 2019-003, 7-18-2019)
815:
(a) Anyone who has not paid the county solid waste assessment fee to the county shall be prohibited from using the county solid waste collection and disposal facilities or any other associated county-operated or provided solid waste facility.
(b) No one shall dispose of solid waste on private or public lands, nor within proper containers provided for the specific type of solid waste unless properly permitted to do so by the environmental protection division of the state department of natural resources.
(c) No business or commercial enterprises shall use any county collection facilities unless specifically authorized. These facilities are solely for the use of residential property owners paying the solid waste assessment fee.
(d) Any person violating any provision of this article shall be subject to a fine not to exceed those presented in section 34-105 or imprisonment for 60 days, or both. Further, it shall be considered a separate violation for each day the violation continues. Jurisdiction shall be in the magistrate court of the county and the procedure for enforcement of such shall be as provided in O.C.G.A.
(Code 1987, § 15-107; Ord. No. 2004-002, 12-7-2004; Ord. No. 2006-002, 2-1-2006)
